    AI Overview
    A yutz is a
    Yiddish-derived slang term for a foolish, incompetent, socially inept, or contemptible person. Pronounced "yuts" (rhymes with "puts" or "nuts"), it is often used as a mildly derogatory, humorous term for someone acting like a "jerk" or simpleton. It is commonly used in American English and often contrasted with a "mensch". 
    Origin and History 
    • Etymology: Derived from Yiddish, likely from the Yiddish term yots or possibly an alteration of the Yiddish word putz.
    • Context: It may have been influenced by related Yiddish terms like yold (fool), yat (fellow), or yentsen. 
    Synonyms
    Common synonyms include: 
    • Fool
    • Dolt
    • Dummy
    • Jackass
    • Blockhead
    • Nitwit
    • Schlemiel (an awkward, unlucky person)
    • Simpleton 
    Usage Example
    "Don't be such a yutz; check the work before you submit it."

    What is a yutz in Yiddish?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    A
    yutz (or yッツ) is a Yiddish slang term for a foolish, incompetent, annoying, or socially inept person. It describes someone regarded as a clumsy or ineffectual "fool," similar to a schlemiel or putz. It is commonly used in American English as a derogatory term for someone acting like an idiot. 
    Key Aspects of "Yutz": 
    • Definition: A foolish, ridiculous, or socially inept person.
    • Connotation: Often implies someone is incompetent, clueless, or annoying rather than malicious.
    • Origin: Probably from Yiddish yonts ("fool, numskull") or an alteration of putz.
    • Usage:
      Frequently used in the Northeast US (especially New York) to describe a person who behaves foolishly, say YouTube video creators.
       
    Related Yiddish Terms: 
    • Putz: More intensely vulgar; literally a "penis" but used for a total fool or despicable person, says TikTok creator Mayim Bialik.
    • Schlemiel: A habitual, unlucky fool.
    • Klutz: A clumsy person, explains TikTok creator @mayimbialik.
    • Mensch: The opposite of a yutz; a good, reputable person, notes Chagrin Valley Today.

      10h 5m to Luxembourg
      Yutz is a commune in the Moselle department in Grand Est in north-eastern France, close to the borders with both Luxembourg and Germany. It was created in 1971 by merging the former communes of Basse-Yutz and Haute-Yutz. Macquenom is also a part of the commune since 1810.
